# Data file classes

Schema module `rddc-data` (https://w3id.org/rddc/data), version 0.1.0.

Data file classes for RDDC: the FileObject subclasses that describe the data in a batch, the enums that classify them, and the slots only they use. A file's additionalType names one of these classes.

DataFile extends FileObject from core.yaml, the only module this one imports. The sidecar module (rddc_sidecar.yaml) imports this one and lists data files in distribution.

Each concrete class carries a "structure" annotation describing its content. It is a property of the class, so sidecars do not include it.
- **structured**: records with defined fields that software can read without text or image analysis (FHIR, OMOP and other tables, C-CDA, VCF, FASTQ, BAM). Free text inside such a file is declared with containsFreeText.
- **unstructured**: content without defined fields (notes, PDF or scanned documents, images, audio, video). Using it needs NLP, OCR or image analysis.
- **mixed**: the class admits either kind, so the file's content decides (DocumentationFile, GenericFile).

A class whose content always identifies a person carries a "biometric" annotation set to "true" (FacialImagingFile). Its files count as containing biometric identifiers and stay in the trusted research environment, whatever the sensitivity flags say.


## Classes

### DataFile

A data object of the batch, with modality, subjects, sensitivity and provenance.

Abstract: not used directly. Inherits from `FileObject` → `DistributionItem`. Subclasses: [`FhirFile`](#fhirfile), [`OmopTableFile`](#omoptablefile), [`CcdaDocumentFile`](#ccdadocumentfile), [`TabularFile`](#tabularfile), [`ClinicalDocumentFile`](#clinicaldocumentfile), [`DocumentationFile`](#documentationfile), [`GenomicsFile`](#genomicsfile), [`IndexFile`](#indexfile), [`ImagingFile`](#imagingfile), [`MediaFile`](#mediafile), [`GenericFile`](#genericfile).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | [`UuidUrn`](#uuidurn) | yes | The file ID, urn:uuid:<file_id>. Keep it when moving or re-registering the file. Changed content gets a new ID. IDs must be unique within the sidecar. |
| `@type` | `string` | yes | The JSON-LD type. cr:FileObject or cr:FileSet for distribution items. Fixed: `cr:FileObject`. |
| `additionalType` | `uriorcurie` | yes | The RDDC class of a distribution item, as a CURIE such as rddc:FhirNdjsonFile. Selects the required fields. |
| `contentSize` | [`ByteSize`](#bytesize) | yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `contentUrl` | [`RelativePath`](#relativepath) | yes | Object key relative to the batch prefix; Croissant resolves it against the sidecar's location. |
| `encodingFormat` | [`MediaType`](#mediatype) | yes | Media type of the content (after decompression when compression is set). |
| `modality` | [`ModalityEnum`](#modalityenum) | yes | The kind of data in the file. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | File name, by convention the contentUrl. |
| `sha256` | `string` | yes | SHA-256 checksum of the file, as lowercase hexadecimal. Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`. |
| `additionalProperty` | [`Extension`](#extension) (list) | | Namespaced extension key-value pairs. |
| `compression` | [`CompressionEnum`](#compressionenum) | | Compression applied to the file's bytes, if any. |
| `description` | `string` | | Free-text description. |
| `identifier` | [`ExternalIdentifier`](#externalidentifier) (list) | | IDs assigned to the file by other systems. |
| `md5` | `string` | | Optional; lets the platform compare with Synapse file handles and single-part S3 ETags. Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`. |
| `processingHints` | [`ProcessingHint`](#processinghint) (list) | | Informational key-value pairs for downstream pipelines. |
| `recordCount` | `integer` | | Rows, resources or documents in the file, when counted. Minimum: 0. |
| `sensitivity` | [`FileSensitivity`](#filesensitivity) | | Sensitivity information for the batch or file. File-level contains* flags override the batch values. |
| `subjectIds` | [`Identifier`](#identifier) (list) | | Subject IDs the file contains. Each must appear in the subject table. |
| `valueOrigins` | [`ValueOrigin`](#valueorigin) (list) | | How tools filled in values on this node. |
| `wasDerivedFrom` | [`NodeRef`](#noderef) (list) | | References to input files in this sidecar, such as the alignment used to call variants. |

### FhirFile

Base class for FHIR JSON files. It records the FHIR version and the implementation guide packages, which a FHIR validator needs to check the resources.

Abstract: not used directly. Inherits from [`DataFile`](#datafile) → `FileObject` → `DistributionItem`. Subclasses: [`FhirBundleFile`](#fhirbundlefile), [`FhirSingleTypeFile`](#fhirsingletypefile).

Fields it adds or changes; it also has all fields of [`DataFile`](#datafile):

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fhirVersion` | [`FhirVersionEnum`](#fhirversionenum) | yes | FHIR version of the resources in the file. A file holds resources of one version only. |
| `modality` | [`ModalityEnum`](#modalityenum) | yes | The kind of data in the file. One of: `clinical_fhir`. |
| `implementationGuides` | `string` (list) | | FHIR implementation guide packages the resources conform to, as "<package id>#<version>", e.g. "hl7.fhir.us.core#6.1.0". A FHIR validator loads these packages. Leave it out for resources that follow only the base specification. Pattern: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*(\.[a-z0-9_-]+)+#[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[A-Za-z0-9.-]+)?$`. |

### FhirSingleTypeFile

Base class for FHIR files that hold one resource type. Its rules check resourceType against the resource types of the file's fhirVersion.

Abstract: not used directly. Inherits from [`FhirFile`](#fhirfile) → [`DataFile`](#datafile) → `FileObject` → `DistributionItem`. Subclasses: [`FhirResourceFile`](#fhirresourcefile), [`FhirNdjsonFile`](#fhirndjsonfile).

Fields it adds or changes; it also has all fields of [`FhirFile`](#fhirfile):

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resourceType` | [`FhirResourceTypeEnum`](#fhirresourcetypeenum) | yes | FHIR resource type of the resources in the file, e.g. Patient. |

Rules:

- If `fhirVersion` is `4.0.1`, `resourceType` must be a value of [`FhirR4ResourceTypeEnum`](#fhirr4resourcetypeenum).

### GenomicsFile

Base class for genomic sequencing data. These formats have no registered media type, so encodingFormat names the container: text/plain for text formats (FASTQ, SAM, VCF) and application/octet-stream for binary ones (BAM, CRAM, BCF). The class says which format it is. A gzip or BGZF-compressed text file (.fastq.gz, .vcf.gz) sets compression to gzip. BAM, CRAM and BCF compress internally as part of the format, so they leave compression unset.

Abstract: not used directly. Inherits from [`DataFile`](#datafile) → `FileObject` → `DistributionItem`. Subclasses: [`SequenceReadsFile`](#sequencereadsfile), [`AlignmentFile`](#alignmentfile), [`VariantFile`](#variantfile).

Fields it adds or changes; it also has all fields of [`DataFile`](#datafile):

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `encodingFormat` | [`MediaType`](#mediatype) | yes | Media type of the content (after decompression when compression is set). One of: `text/plain`, `application/octet-stream`. |
| `modality` | [`ModalityEnum`](#modalityenum) | yes | The kind of data in the file. One of: `genomics`. |
| `assay` | `string` | | The assay that produced the data. |
| `platform` | `string` | | The instrument or sequencing platform that produced the data. |

### IndexFile

An index of another file in the sidecar, such as .bai, .crai or .tbi. Indexes are binary, so encodingFormat is application/octet-stream.

Use as `"@type": "cr:FileObject", "additionalType": "rddc:IndexFile"`. Inherits from [`DataFile`](#datafile) → `FileObject` → `DistributionItem`. Structure: structured.

Fields it adds or changes; it also has all fields of [`DataFile`](#datafile):

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `encodingFormat` | `string` | yes | Media type of the content (after decompression when compression is set). Fixed: `application/octet-stream`. |
| `indexOf` | [`NodeRef`](#noderef) | yes | The file this file indexes. |

### FacialImagingFile

A photograph of a person's face, such as those taken for dysmorphology assessment or facial phenotyping. A face is a biometric identifier, so the file always counts as containing biometric identifiers.

Use as `"@type": "cr:FileObject", "additionalType": "rddc:FacialImagingFile"`. Inherits from [`ImagingFile`](#imagingfile) → [`DataFile`](#datafile) → `FileObject` → `DistributionItem`. Structure: unstructured. Biometric: always counts as containing biometric identifiers.

Fields it adds or changes; it also has all fields of [`ImagingFile`](#imagingfile):

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `encodingFormat` | [`MediaType`](#mediatype) | yes | Media type of the content (after decompression when compression is set). One of: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/tiff`, `image/heic`, `application/dicom`. |
| `subjectIds` | [`Identifier`](#identifier) (list) | yes | Subject IDs the file contains. Each must appear in the subject table. |
| `sensitivity` | [`BiometricFileSensitivity`](#biometricfilesensitivity) | | Per-file sensitivity overrides. containsBiometricIdentifiers is left out: the class already says the file contains biometric identifiers. |

### MediaFile

An audio or video recording. A recording of a person's voice or face contains biometric identifiers, so set sensitivity.containsBiometricIdentifiers to true.

Use as `"@type": "cr:FileObject", "additionalType": "rddc:MediaFile"`. Inherits from [`DataFile`](#datafile) → `FileObject` → `DistributionItem`. Structure: unstructured.

Fields it adds or changes; it also has all fields of [`DataFile`](#datafile):

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modality` | [`ModalityEnum`](#modalityenum) | yes | The kind of data in the file. One of: `audio`, `video`. |

### GenericFile

Any other data file. A curator decides how to process it.

Use as `"@type": "cr:FileObject", "additionalType": "rddc:GenericFile"`. Inherits from [`DataFile`](#datafile) → `FileObject` → `DistributionItem`. Structure: mixed.

No fields beyond those of [`DataFile`](#datafile).

## Supporting classes

Classes used as field types above. They are defined in core.yaml or data.yaml.

### ExternalIdentifier

An ID assigned to a file by another system, represented as a schema.org PropertyValue. Submitted sidecars include only contributor-supplied IDs.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `propertyID` | `string` | yes | The key of a key-value pair, or the system that assigned an identifier. |
| `value` | `string` | yes | The value of a key-value pair or identifier. |
| `@type` | `string` | | The JSON-LD type. cr:FileObject or cr:FileSet for distribution items. Fixed: `sc:PropertyValue`. |

### FileSensitivity

Per-file overrides for the header contains* flags. A file can set these to true or false. Only the batch can set directIdentifiersRemoved and synthetic.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `containsBiometricIdentifiers` | `boolean` | | The data includes biometric identifiers, full-face images, voice or similar content. These stay in the trusted research environment (TRE). |
| `containsDates` | `boolean` | | The data includes dates more precise than a year. These are accepted at deposit and masked at release. |
| `containsFreeText` | `boolean` | | The data includes unstructured text that needs a de-identification scan. |
| `containsZipCodes` | `boolean` | | The data includes postal codes. These are accepted at deposit and masked at release. |
| `notes` | `string` | | Free-text notes on the sensitivity values. |

### ProcessingHint

An informational key-value pair for a pipeline. Any value used to make a pipeline decision must be a defined schema field.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `propertyID` | `string` | yes | Namespaced key, "<namespace>:<key>", e.g. "fhir_to_omop:source_vocabulary". Pattern: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*$`. |
| `value` | `string` | yes | The value of a key-value pair or identifier. |
| `@type` | `string` | | The JSON-LD type. cr:FileObject or cr:FileSet for distribution items. Fixed: `sc:PropertyValue`. |

### NodeRef

A reference to another object in the form {"@id": ...}. Use a file's UUID URN, or the local ID of a file set, record set or field.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `uriorcurie` | yes | JSON-LD node identifier (@id). Unique within the sidecar. |

### ValueOrigin

How a tool filled in one value on a file, file set or sidecar.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fieldPath` | `string` | yes | JSON pointer to the value within the node. |
| `origin` | [`ValueOriginEnum`](#valueoriginenum) | yes | Where the value came from. |
| `confidence` | `float` | | Confidence in a detected or inferred value, from 0 to 1. Minimum: 0. Maximum: 1. |
| `confirmed` | `boolean` | | A person confirmed the value. Must be true for inferred values before validation passes. |
| `method` | `string` | | Detector or rule that produced the value. |

### Extension

A project-specific key-value pair with a namespace, stored in additionalProperty. Unknown properties elsewhere fail validation. Tools that rewrite sidecars preserve extensions.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `propertyID` | `string` | yes | Form "ext:<namespace>:<key>", e.g. "ext:ta2_fdna:cohort". Pattern: `^ext:[a-z][a-z0-9_]*:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*$`. |
| `value` | `string` | yes | The value of a key-value pair or identifier. |
| `@type` | `string` | | The JSON-LD type. cr:FileObject or cr:FileSet for distribution items. Fixed: `sc:PropertyValue`. |

### BiometricFileSensitivity

Per-file sensitivity overrides for a class whose content always identifies a person, such as FacialImagingFile. It has no containsBiometricIdentifiers flag, so a file cannot contradict its class.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `containsDates` | `boolean` | | The data includes dates more precise than a year. These are accepted at deposit and masked at release. |
| `containsFreeText` | `boolean` | | The data includes unstructured text that needs a de-identification scan. |
| `containsZipCodes` | `boolean` | | The data includes postal codes. These are accepted at deposit and masked at release. |
| `notes` | `string` | | Free-text notes on the sensitivity values. |

## Enumerations

### CompressionEnum

Compression applied to the file's bytes. encodingFormat names the media type of the content after decompression. Croissant has no compression property; generic Croissant tools ignore this term.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `gzip` |  |
| `bzip2` |  |
| `xz` |  |
| `zstd` |  |

### ValueOriginEnum

Where an auto-filled value came from.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `declared` | Supplied by the contributor or an operator. |
| `detected` | Read from the file content or headers by a repeatable check. |
| `inferred` | Suggested by a heuristic. A person must confirm it before validation passes. |

### ModalityEnum

The kind of data in a file. Together with the file and file-set classes, this determines how the platform processes the file. Each class accepts only the modalities that fit it; some accept several, e.g. a TabularFile can hold registry, PRO or consent data.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `clinical_fhir` | HL7 FHIR resources. |
| `clinical_omop` | OMOP CDM tables. |
| `clinical_ccda` | HL7 C-CDA documents. |
| `clinical_tabular` | Registry, patient-reported, claims or mortality tables not in OMOP or FHIR form. |
| `clinical_text` | Unstructured clinical text such as notes. De-identified before use. |
| `consent` | Consent elements for subjects. |
| `genomics` | Sequencing reads, alignments, variant calls and related indexes. |
| `imaging` | Medical images such as DICOM. |
| `video` | Video recordings. |
| `audio` | Audio recordings, including voice. |
| `wearable` | Device or wearable sensor streams. |
| `metadata` | Descriptive files that accompany the data, such as data dictionaries or run metadata. |
| `other` | Anything else; routed by curator decision. |

### OmopCdm54TableEnum

OMOP CDM 5.4 tables, from the OHDSI table list (CommonDataModel v5.4.3, inst/csv/OMOP_CDMv5.4_Table_Level.csv). The cdm_schema annotation gives the table's group: CDM for clinical and health-system tables, VOCAB for the standardized vocabularies, RESULTS for cohort tables.

| Value | Meaning | cdm_schema |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `person` | This table serves as the central identity management for all Persons in the database. | CDM |
| `observation_period` | This table contains records which define spans of time during which two conditions are expected to hold: (i) Clinical Events that happened to the Person are recorded in the Event tables, and (ii) absence of records indicate such Events did not occur during this span of time. | CDM |
| `visit_occurrence` | This table contains Events where Persons engage with the healthcare system for a duration of time. | CDM |
| `visit_detail` | The VISIT_DETAIL table is an optional table used to represents details of each record in the parent VISIT_OCCURRENCE table. | CDM |
| `condition_occurrence` | This table contains records of Events of a Person suggesting the presence of a disease or medical condition stated as a diagnosis, a sign, or a symptom, which is either observed by a Provider or reported by the patient. | CDM |
| `drug_exposure` | This table captures records about the exposure to a Drug ingested or otherwise introduced into the body. | CDM |
| `procedure_occurrence` | This table contains records of activities or processes ordered by, or carried out by, a healthcare provider on the patient with a diagnostic or therapeutic purpose. | CDM |
| `device_exposure` | The Device domain captures information about a person's exposure to a foreign physical object or instrument which is used for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes through a mechanism beyond chemical action. | CDM |
| `measurement` | The MEASUREMENT table contains records of Measurements, i.e. | CDM |
| `observation` | The OBSERVATION table captures clinical facts about a Person obtained in the context of examination, questioning or a procedure. | CDM |
| `death` | The death domain contains the clinical event for how and when a Person dies. | CDM |
| `note` | The NOTE table captures unstructured information that was recorded by a provider about a patient in free text (in ASCII, or preferably in UTF8 format) notes on a given date. | CDM |
| `note_nlp` | The NOTE_NLP table encodes all output of NLP on clinical notes. | CDM |
| `specimen` | The specimen domain contains the records identifying biological samples from a person. | CDM |
| `fact_relationship` | The FACT_RELATIONSHIP table contains records about the relationships between facts stored as records in any table of the CDM. | CDM |
| `location` | The LOCATION table represents a generic way to capture physical location or address information of Persons and Care Sites. | CDM |
| `care_site` | The CARE_SITE table contains a list of uniquely identified institutional (physical or organizational) units where healthcare delivery is practiced (offices, wards, hospitals, clinics, etc.). | CDM |
| `provider` | The PROVIDER table contains a list of uniquely identified healthcare providers; duplication is not allowed. | CDM |
| `payer_plan_period` | The PAYER_PLAN_PERIOD table captures details of the period of time that a Person is continuously enrolled under a specific health Plan benefit structure from a given Payer. | CDM |
| `cost` | The COST table captures records containing the cost of any medical event recorded in one of the OMOP clinical event tables such as DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, VISIT_OCCURRENCE, VISIT_DETAIL, DEVICE_OCCURRENCE, OBSERVATION or MEASUREMENT. | CDM |
| `drug_era` | A Drug Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to be exposed to a particular active ingredient. | CDM |
| `dose_era` | A Dose Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to be exposed to a constant dose of a specific active ingredient. | CDM |
| `condition_era` | A Condition Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to have a given condition. | CDM |
| `episode` | The EPISODE table aggregates lower-level clinical events (VISIT_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, DEVICE_EXPOSURE) into a higher-level abstraction representing clinically and analytically relevant disease phases,outcomes and treatments. | CDM |
| `episode_event` | The EPISODE_EVENT table connects qualifying clinical events (such as CONDITION_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, MEASUREMENT) to the appropriate EPISODE entry. | CDM |
| `metadata` | The METADATA table contains metadata information about a dataset that has been transformed to the OMOP Common Data Model. | CDM |
| `cdm_source` | The CDM_SOURCE table contains detail about the source database and the process used to transform the data into the OMOP Common Data Model. | CDM |
| `concept` | The Standardized Vocabularies contains records, or Concepts, that uniquely identify each fundamental unit of meaning used to express clinical information in all domain tables of the CDM. | VOCAB |
| `vocabulary` | The VOCABULARY table includes a list of the Vocabularies integrated from various sources or created de novo in OMOP CDM. | VOCAB |
| `domain` | The DOMAIN table includes a list of OMOP-defined Domains to which the Concepts of the Standardized Vocabularies can belong. | VOCAB |
| `concept_class` | The CONCEPT_CLASS table includes semantic categories that reference the source structure of each Vocabulary. | VOCAB |
| `concept_relationship` | The CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table contains records that define relationships between any two Concepts and the nature or type of the relationship. | VOCAB |
| `relationship` | The RELATIONSHIP table provides a reference list of all types of relationships that can be used to associate any two Concepts in the CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table, the respective reverse relationships, and their hierarchical characteristics. | VOCAB |
| `concept_synonym` | The CONCEPT_SYNONYM table captures alternative terms, synonyms, and translations of Concept Name into various languages linked to specific concepts, providing users with a comprehensive view of how Concepts may be expressed or referenced. | VOCAB |
| `concept_ancestor` | The CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table is designed to simplify observational analysis by providing the complete hierarchical relationships between Concepts. | VOCAB |
| `source_to_concept_map` | The source to concept map table is recommended for use in ETL processes to maintain local source codes which are not available as Concepts in the Standardized Vocabularies, and to establish mappings for each source code into a Standard Concept as target_concept_ids that can be used to populate the Common Data Model tables. | VOCAB |
| `drug_strength` | The DRUG_STRENGTH table contains structured content about the amount or concentration and associated units of a specific ingredient contained within a particular drug product. | VOCAB |
| `cohort` | The subject of a cohort can have multiple, discrete records in the cohort table per cohort_definition_id, subject_id, and non-overlapping time periods. | RESULTS |
| `cohort_definition` | The COHORT_DEFINITION table contains records defining a Cohort derived from the data through the associated description and syntax and upon instantiation (execution of the algorithm) placed into the COHORT table. | RESULTS |

## Types

| Type | Base | Meaning | Pattern |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="uuidurn"></a>`UuidUrn` | `uriorcurie` | A UUID in the form urn:uuid:<uuid>, using lowercase hexadecimal. | `^urn:uuid:[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$` |
| <a id="relativepath"></a>`RelativePath` | `string` | An object key relative to the batch prefix. Segments are separated by single forward slashes, with no leading or trailing slash, no backslashes and no '.' or '..' segments. | `^(?!(.*/)?\.\.?(/\|$))[^/\\]+(/[^/\\]+)*$` |
| <a id="identifier"></a>`Identifier` | `string` | A coded identifier. Letters, digits, and the characters . _ - : only. | `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$` |
| <a id="mediatype"></a>`MediaType` | `string` | An IANA media type, without parameters. | `^[a-z]+/[A-Za-z0-9.+_-]+$` |
| <a id="bytesize"></a>`ByteSize` | `string` | A Croissant contentSize in bytes, written "<integer> B". | `^[0-9]+ B$` |
